title: What the practical expects
intro: You need to recognize taxa quickly, explain the feature that supports each ID, and link the feature to anatomy or ecology.

cards.heading: Observe
cards.title: Find the feature
cards.detail: Look for a visible character before naming the group.

cards.heading: Group
cards.title: Choose the smallest defensible unit
cards.detail: Order or suborder first; family only when the key is supplied.

cards.heading: Explain
cards.title: State the evidence
cards.detail: Name the diagnostic trait and what it means.

title: External anatomy
intro: Focus on the head, thorax, legs, and abdomen. Learn where structures sit and what they do before working through taxonomic identifications.

cards.heading: Head
cards.title: compound eyes, ocellus, antennae
cards.detail: Sensory input and sight.

cards.heading: Mouthparts
cards.title: labrum, mandibles, maxilla, labium
cards.detail: Feeding structures and function.

cards.heading: Thorax
cards.title: prothorax, mesothorax, metathorax
cards.detail: Leg and wing attachment points.

cards.heading: Abdomen
cards.title: spiracles, cerci, terga, sterna
cards.detail: Breathing and posterior structures.

title: Internal anatomy
intro: Internal anatomy is usually less about huge memorization and more about the relationship between structure and function: respiration, circulation, digestion, and neural coordination.

cards.heading: Circulation
cards.title: heart + aorta + dorsal vessel
cards.detail: Moves hemolymph through the body.

cards.heading: Respiration
cards.title: tracheae, tracheoles, taenidia
cards.detail: Delivers oxygen to tissues.

cards.heading: Digestion
cards.title: crop, ventriculus, Malpighian tubules
cards.detail: Processes and moves nutrients and waste.

title: Legs, wings, mouthparts & antennae
intro: Learn the basic type, its function, and what feature distinguishes it from a similar structure.

cards.heading: Legs
cards.title: saltatorial, fossorial, raptorial, natatorial
cards.detail: Jumping, digging, grasping, swimming.

cards.heading: Wings
cards.title: tegmina, elytra, hemelytra, fringed wings
cards.detail: Leathery, membranous, or fringe-winged forms.

cards.heading: Antennae
cards.title: serrate, plumose, filiform, geniculate
cards.detail: Saw-like, feather-like, thread-like, elbowed.

title: Taxonomic hierarchy and major groups
intro: Keep the hierarchy clear: order, suborder, family, and grouping. The practical likely expects you to identify a group by a combination of characters rather than a single detail.

cards.heading: Major groups
cards.title: Apterygote, Paleoptera, Neoptera
cards.detail: Primitive and derived lineages.

cards.heading: Orders
cards.title: Ephemeroptera, Odonata, Orthoptera, Hemiptera
cards.detail: Use orders as the core recognition target.

cards.heading: Suborders
cards.title: Zygoptera, Anisoptera, Ensifera, Heteroptera
cards.detail: Look for the correct subordinate grouping.

title: Orders & suborders: how to recognize them
intro: A strong answer usually names the specific trait that distinguishes one order or suborder from the others. Practice from a clue to the taxon, then reverse it and say why the answer matches.

cards.heading: Odonata
cards.title: strong flyers, aquatic nymphs, hinged mask
cards.detail: Often obvious by wing plan and predatory nymphs.

cards.heading: Orthoptera
cards.title: saltatorial hind legs, tegmina, tympana
cards.detail: Classic jumping grasshopper and cricket clues.

cards.heading: Hemiptera
cards.title: piercing-sucking beak, often hemelytra or wings
cards.detail: A beak and stylized mouthparts are the key giveaway.

title: Polyneoptera & Dictyoptera
intro: These groups are best recognized by the combination of morphology and life history. Focus on wing form, mouthparts, and the presence of a distinctive body plan or feeding habit.

cards.heading: Polyneoptera
cards.title: Orthoptera, Phasmatodea, Dermaptera, Plecoptera
cards.detail: Diverse assemblage with major morphological variation.

cards.heading: Dictyoptera
cards.title: Blattodea, Mantodea
cards.detail: Commonly recognized by body plan and forewing features.

title: Hemiptera and its suborders
intro: Learn the three suborders and the common family-level key characters that the supplied keys rely on in practice.

cards.heading: Sternorrhyncha
cards.title: aphids, scale insects
cards.detail: Often soft-bodied and plant-feeding.

cards.heading: Auchenorrhyncha
cards.title: cicadas, leafhoppers
cards.detail: Membranous wings and hind leg/wing patterns often matter.

cards.heading: Heteroptera
cards.title: true bugs
cards.detail: Beak-based predators and plant feeders, often with hemelytra.

title: Families: what features the provided keys use
intro: The study guide says that they will provide a key for the families, so you don't have to memorize them. The course keys depend on a small set of structures: wing veins, beak segments, abdomen shape, and foreleg specialization.

cards.heading: Odonata key
cards.title: triangle shape, anal loop, wing position
cards.detail: The family key begins with wing characters.

cards.heading: Orthoptera key
cards.title: antenna length, ovipositor, ear position
cards.detail: Suborder-level cues feed into family-level distinctions.

cards.heading: Hemiptera key
cards.title: beak, wing structure, tarsi, cornicles
cards.detail: These are the most common decision points in the family key.

title: Final practical strategy
intro: Start with the biggest visible clue, then narrow down by order, suborder, and any supplied key characters. Do not chase every tiny detail: choose the strongest, most identifying trait and explain it.

cards.heading: Step 1
cards.title: Find the main feature
cards.detail: Wing plan, mouthparts, leg type, or body form.

cards.heading: Step 2
cards.title: Match the group
cards.detail: Use the smallest group that fits the evidence.

cards.heading: Step 3
cards.title: State the reason
cards.detail: Explain which characteristic makes that answer strongest.
